title: Read a remainder as a precise statement
chapter: Remainders turn long lists into short systems
goal: Read "remainder r on division by d" as: the number is r more than a multiple of d.

scenes.visual: Group seventeen counters into three rows of five and two loose counters.
scenes.narration: Seventeen counters make three full groups of five, with two left over. That leftover is called the remainder. The three full groups give a multiple of five. The two counters tell you exactly how far seventeen is past that multiple.

scenes.visual: Give each allowable leftover from zero to four a bucket. Slide the fifth counter into a new complete group.
scenes.narration: When we divide whole numbers by five, the possible remainders are zero, one, two, three and four. A leftover of five would make another complete group. However large the starting number, it fits into one of these five remainder classes.

scenes.visual: Build the red, blue, green, yellow strip, label first four positions and ask for bead fifty.
scenes.narration: A necklace repeats red, blue, green and yellow in that order. The first bead is red. What colour is bead fifty? Try marking the boundaries between the repeating groups of four.

scenes.visual: Compress twelve cycles into twelve tiles and unfold two positions of cycle thirteen.
scenes.narration: A full cycle has four beads. Fifty is twelve groups of four, plus two more beads. The twelve groups take us to bead forty-eight. Count two beads into the next cycle. Its second colour is blue, so bead fifty is blue.

scenes.visual: Move the cursor back to the end of a complete cycle. Highlight the last bead and remainder zero.
scenes.narration: Bead forty-eight lands on a complete group boundary. It has remainder zero when divided by four. In this position list we count from one, so a complete group finishes on its fourth bead. Bead forty-eight is yellow.

scenes.visual: Align two group strips for 23 and 38. Cancel their shared residue and show three extra groups of five.
scenes.narration: Twenty-three is four groups of five plus three. Thirty-eight is seven groups of five plus three. In the difference, the two leftovers cancel. Three extra groups of five give fifteen. And adding any whole group of five leaves a remainder unchanged. That is why equal remainders and a multiple-of-five difference go together.

scenes.visual: Place the six candidates on a number line. Sort them by remainder modulo three, then identify the two in the target column.
scenes.narration: Try combining two conditions. Below thirty, the numbers with remainder three on division by five are three, eight, thirteen, eighteen, twenty-three and twenty-eight. Now test them for remainder one on division by three. Only thirteen and twenty-eight reach that column.

scenes.visual: Return to a full group plus leftover, then show the Tuesday and one hundred days problem.
scenes.narration: A remainder tells how far you are past a multiple. It must be smaller than the divisor. For a repeating pattern, decide which position sits at remainder zero. Here is your notebook challenge. Today is Tuesday. What day will it be one hundred days from now?

notebook_exercise: Today is Tuesday. What day will it be 100 days from now?
notebook_answer: 100 = 7 x 14 + 2, so two days after Tuesday: Thursday.
